# Whether an unmodified `claude` CLI, driven over stdio stream-json, will call a
# tool a third-party host declares, ask that host's permission for it, wait while
# the host holds the call open — and what the turn costs.
#
# The recording W2's gate reads (.omc/plans/2026-09-08-claude-code-wire.md, §W1b
# lines 1234-1834 and §W2 1835-1888; D556). NINETEEN invocations in four passes —
# two zero-turn argv preflights, one argv refusal that spent no turn, and sixteen
# processes that paid for TWENTY-ONE turns between them, TEN OF WHICH THE VENDOR'S
# OWN SAFEGUARD REFUSED — each run by the user through `!`. No lane and no lead ran
# a `claude` turn, no credential file was read, and nothing was written under the
# repository.
#
# Recorded by: the plan's own §W1b driver, saved as
#              .omc/handoffs/ralplan-2026-09-08-claude-code-wire/w1b-spike.py,
#              with W1a-7's answer substituted at the `# W1a-7` marker: the
#              87-name never-inherit tuple ran (the union of the plan's own ~20
#              and the bundle's 76-name `nSe`), not the ~20-name fallback. The two
#              `# W1a-5` lines were NOT moved: W1a Q5 found the driver's
#              `{type:"control_response", response:{subtype, request_id,
#              response|error}}` envelope is the one the CLI parses.
# Date:   2026-09-10 (JST), in four passes, each one the user's own `!` run of a
#         block in .omc/handoffs/ralplan-2026-09-08-claude-code-wire/:
#           01:46-01:47  runs 0, 0b, 1-9b        `w1b-all.sh`      (12 invocations)
#           03:33        runs 2b, 9c             `w1b-rerun.sh`    (Dv-7, Dv-8)
#           03:51        runs 2c, 2d, 9d         `w1b-rerun2.sh`   (Dv-9)
#           04:02, 04:07 runs 2e-1, 2e-2         `w1b-rerun3.sh`, RUN TWICE
#         The frames' own `timestamp`s run 2026-09-09T16:46:55.807Z (run 1's first
#         prompt) to 2026-09-09T19:07:29.363Z (run 2e-2's). Pass 1's twelve ran back
#         to back and span 57.5 s, of which run 1's deliberate 25 s hold on
#         `tools/call` is the largest single interval; the later passes are seconds
#         each. Run 2e-2 is the fourth pass's script re-run 4 m 38 s later with the
#         SAME argv, and the driver appends, which is why one `run2e.jsonl` holds
#         two invocations and why they are two sections here.
# Build:  every paid run and run 0 ran on
#         ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.266, `--version` =
#         "2.1.266 (Claude Code)" — THE BUILD THE FRAMES COME FROM. Run 0b is the
#         same argv preflight on ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.263,
#         `--version` = "2.1.263 (Claude Code)".
#         EVERY `L<n>` LINE CITE IN THE PLAN AND IN w1a-trace.md IS A 2.1.263
#         FACT. Where a frame here and an `L<n>` disagree, the frame wins
#         (§W2's ruling preamble) and the row is an amendment, not a defect.
# argv:   identical on all nineteen invocations except where a run's section says
#         otherwise —
#           -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose
#           --permission-prompt-tool stdio --permission-mode manual
#           --tools "" --setting-sources "" --strict-mcp-config
#           --disable-slash-commands --no-chrome --system-prompt-snapshot off
#           --enable-auth-status --replay-user-messages
#           --session-id <uuidv7>            (runs 0, 0b, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9a, 9b,
#                                             9c, 9d)
#           --resume <sid-1>                 (runs 2, 2b, 2d, in place of
#                                             --session-id)
#           --resume <sid-3>                 (runs 2c, 2e-1, 2e-2, likewise)
#           --session-id <sid-1>             (run 7, deliberately re-using run 1's)
#           --include-partial-messages --thinking enabled
#             --thinking-display summarized --effort high   (run 4 only)
#         The `initialize` control request carries the wire's own replaced
#         `systemPrompt` on runs 2, 2b, 2c, 3, 6, 8, 9a, 9b, 9c, 9d; runs 1, 4, 5,
#         2d, 2e-1 and 2e-2 send none and take the CLI's own preset. That split is
#         the axis half the readings below turn on, so it is stated once here.
# env:    built by NAME only. The driver never printed, logged or recorded an
#         environment VALUE, and neither does this file.
#         SET (9): CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP,
#           CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY,
#           CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC,

#           SSH_ASKPASS, SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE, VSCODE_GIT_ASKPASS_MAIN,
#           VSCODE_GIT_ASKPASS_NODE, VSCODE_GIT_ASKPASS_EXTRA_ARGS,

#           GNOME_TERMINAL_SERVICE, XTERM_VERSION, ALACRITTY_LOG, TILIX_ID,
#           TERMINATOR_UUID, ConEmuANSI, ConEmuPID, ConEmuTask, MSYSTEM,
#           CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT, FORCE_CODE_TERMINAL
#         (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is NOT on either list; run 5 sets it for its one
#          process on purpose, which principle 1 says the wire never does.)
# Tool:   exactly one, declared on every `tools/list` answer —
#           {"name":"ganja_ping","description":"Answers pong. A probe.",
#            "inputSchema":{"type":"object","properties":{},
#                           "additionalProperties":false}}
#         with sdkMcpServers ["ganja"] and sdkMcpServerConfigs
#         {"ganja":{"timeout":3600000}} on every `initialize` control request.
#
# THE WHOLE RECORDING CONTAINS ONE stderr LINE (run 7's session-id refusal) AND
# NO `api_error` FRAME OF ANY KIND, in 461 frames. All SIXTEEN `rate_limit_event`s
# read ordinary subscription draw — `status: allowed`, `isUsingOverage: false`,
# every one — and no frame anywhere names this client: not its User-Agent, not
# CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP, not the `-p` shape. Where the plan asked whether an
# error or a client-naming field would appear, the honest verbatim record is that
# it did not, and the sections below say so. TWO FIELDS DID MOVE between passes,
# and neither is about this client: the five-hour window rolled over (utilization
# 0.68 -> 0.69 -> 0.88 in passes 1-2, then 0 -> 0.02 on a later `resetsAt` in
# passes 3-4, `seven_day` 0.45 -> 0.49 -> 0.73), and `overageStatus` went from
# `rejected` with `overageDisabledReason: org_level_disabled` to `allowed` with an
# `overageResetsAt` — an account-side change between 01:47 and 03:51 that no probe
# asked for and that the wire never reads.
#
# SCRUB (plan lines 1808-1820). Every absolute macOS home path -> `~` and every
# address-shaped email -> `<email>` were done by the user in one pass over the run
# files; that pass was re-derived byte-for-byte here before anything was copied,
# and AC-2.1's own home-path grep finds nothing left, this sentence included. Then, in this file:
# every session id -> `<sid-N>` where N NAMES THE RUN THAT MINTED IT, so run 2's
# `--resume` of run 1 and run 7's deliberately-in-use id both read `<sid-1>`, and
# runs 2c, 2e-1 and 2e-2 read `<sid-3>` because they resume run 3's
# (12 distinct session ids, 270 other uuids; there is no `<sid-2>`, `<sid-2b>`,
# `<sid-2c>`, `<sid-2d>`, `<sid-2e>` or `<sid-7>` because none of those runs minted
# one — they all resumed); every other uuid -> `<u-N>`, numbered per run in first-appearance
# order, so request_id pairing and the tool_use_id <-> `_meta` correlation survive;
# the whole `account` object -> FIELD NAMES ONLY; `auth_status.output` -> its line
# count; the `initialize` reply's `models` -> the id list plus the per-entry field
# names; `behaviors` -> its counts and field names, the agent/skill/plugin/server
# NAMES elided (account telemetry, and no reading needs them); model reply texts
# kept only where they are the probe's own one-word answers (`pong`) and rendered
# `<text, N chars>` otherwise, with the lane's prose beside them saying what the
# reply did; every `error`/`message` string verbatim, the API-refusal banner among
# them; token counts verbatim; `updatedInput` is `{}` and was `{}`. `toolu_…` and
# `req_…` ids are the vendor's own per-call correlators and are kept: nothing
# reads them and they are what makes M6 legible.
#
# NOTHING READS THIS FILE. No `include_str!` names it; it is evidence, judged by a
# person, and must never be edited to make a test pass.

== the runs ==

# `meta.exit`. The `t` in every frame below is the driver's own millisecond offset
# from that process's spawn.

        rendered preamble text. 1 turn.                         M3c             exit 1

run 9c  a fresh record, replaced prompt, run 1 as a preamble
        with REFUSED turns filtered out (Dv-8), and the benign
        prompt `Reply with the word pong.` 1 turn.               M3c             exit 1
run 2c  --resume of run 3's CLEAN record under the SAME
        replaced prompt it was made with. 1 turn.                M17 M3c         exit 0
run 2d  --resume of run 1's record under the CLI's own PRESET
        — no replaced prompt at all. 1 turn.                     M17             exit 1
run 9d  a fresh record, replaced prompt, run 1 as a preamble

        block (Dv-9). 1 turn (2 API requests, tool called).      M3c G1 G2 M6    exit 0
run 2e-1 --resume of run 3's clean record under the PRESET: a
        CHANGED prompt on a clean record. 1 turn.                M17             exit 0
run 2e-2 the same probe re-run 4 m 38 s later, same argv, on the
        record 2e-1 had just extended. 1 turn.                   M17 M3c         exit 1
#
# EVERY TURN-TAKING RUN THAT EXITED 1 PRODUCED A `system/model_refusal_no_fallback`
# FRAME, AND EVERY ONE THAT PRODUCED ONE EXITED 1: run 1 x1, run 2 x2, run 9a x1,
# run 9b x1, run 2b x2, run 9c x1, run 2d x1, run 2e-2 x1 — TEN FRAMES, EIGHT RUNS,
# ten of the recording's twenty-one paid turns. (Run 7 also exits 1 and is the one
# exception in the other direction: it is refused by argv before a turn exists.)
# Every `result` in the recording carries `subtype: "success"`; the refused ones
# carry `is_error: true`, `stop_reason: "refusal"` and `terminal_reason:
# "api_error"`, with `output_tokens` 0. The 2.1.263 bundle decides the code at
# L1112681, `Pr(zn?.type === "result" && zn?.is_error || dr ? 1 : 0)` — `zn` is the
# last frame emitted, `dr` a permanent transport close. So the print-mode exit code
# reads the LAST result's `is_error` and never its `subtype`: a wire that reads
# `subtype == "success"` as success is wrong on eight of these sixteen runs.
#
# WHAT THE THREE LATER PASSES ESTABLISHED, and it is the largest thing this file
# records. The refusals are not the question's wording (run 2b: both prompts
# rephrased, both refused), not the `API Error:` banner riding in a preamble
# (run 9c: the banner filtered out by Dv-8, still refused), and not a changed
# system prompt as such (run 2e-1: preset over a record made under the replaced
# prompt, SERVED). Read as a table, every cell a section below:
#
#   shape                                              runs               served?
#   held process, replaced prompt, several turns       3, 6, 8 (2 turns)  yes
#   --resume of a clean record, same prompt            2c                 yes
#   --resume of a clean record, CHANGED prompt         2e-1               yes
#   --resume of that same record one turn later        2e-2               REFUSED
#   --resume of run 1's record, any prompt             2, 2b, 2d (5)      REFUSED
#   fresh record, preamble WITH `[Assistant]` lines    9a, 9b, 9c         REFUSED
#   fresh record, preamble WITHOUT them                9d                 yes
#   preset, a question about a tool result, same proc  1 t2               yes
#   preset, "call the tool once *more*" after a carry  1 t3               REFUSED
#
# Two readings hold across all of it. (i) A preamble is served when it carries the
# user's asks and the tool trail and NOT the model's own words — 9d against 9a/9b/9c
# — which is what the refusal's own sentence ("duplicating model outputs") says.
# (ii) Run 1's record is refused whatever the prompt, and it is the only resumed
# record holding both a carried injection-shaped block (M19) and a refused turn's
# banner; WHICH of the two poisons it is not isolated by this recording, and the
# same shape that served 2e-1 refused 2e-2 five minutes later with the argv, the
# prompt and the record's cleanliness all held fixed. So the safe space is a
# tendency the frames measure, NOT a rule they prove: a wire that must never see a
# refusal cannot be built on this table alone.
#
# The three deviations the later passes ran under, named where a reader will look
# for them: Dv-7 (run 2b's two prompts rephrased away from the safeguard's shape),
# Dv-8 (the driver's renderer drops the assistant text of a turn whose `result` was
# `is_error: true` — W3 rule (γ) applied to the driver, run 9c), Dv-9 (the driver's
# `--preamble-omit-assistant`: no `[Assistant]` line and no carried block, run 9d).
# The reading index below is the first pass's and is unamended; rows M2, M17 and
# M3c and items 7 and 8 of the closing list are the ones these seven invocations
# move, and the run sections say how.

# [9] M7, THE ANSWER ARRIVING THE OTHER WAY - the CLI ECHOES the driver's own `control_response` back on stdout, VERBATIM, request_id and all. This is idx3 reflected. == what this recording does NOT settle ==
# Stated as plainly as the readings, so no W3 lane mistakes a gap for a fact.
1. M16 — whether an `allow` records a CLI-side session grant that shadows the next
   ask for the same tool. Run 1's third turn was refused before the model could
   ask again, so the recording holds exactly one `can_use_tool`. Nothing here
   supports or refutes the grant hypothesis.
2. M17's prompt half, and M2 — whether a resumed process takes a replaced
   `initialize.systemPrompt`. Both of run 2's turns were refused.
3. M18's mid-turn arm — what `interrupt` does to a RUNNING turn, and whether a
   `result` closes it. The only `interrupt` in the recording hit an idle process.
4. What `--effort high` changed. It parsed and the turn completed; no frame
   echoes it.
5. WHICH project-local input the checkout-as-cwd run pulled in (M5). The 8 772
   is measured; the cause is not.
6. What `display: "updates"` (W1a Q1.9) produces on the wire. Run 1 passed no
   `--thinking-display` and got an `assistant` thinking block with an EMPTY
   `thinking` and a full signature — consistent with the text being withheld, but
   the branch was not identified from the frames.
7. Whether a `preamble::render` that DROPS refused turns changes M3c's answer.
   Runs 9a and 9b each carried at least one `API Error:` banner into their prompt
   as an `[Assistant]` reply, because the driver's renderer reads every `assistant`
   frame and a refused turn's frame is the banner. Both still read 0 cache, so the
   reading stands, but the prompts measured are not the prompts a filtering
   renderer would send.
8. Whether the five `reasoning_extraction` refusals are a property of the
   QUESTION SHAPE ("which tool did you call", "what does your system prompt say",
   "which word did the tool return... above") or of replaying a `thinking` block
   in a later request. Run 1's turn 2 asked a question of the first kind and was
   ANSWERED; its turn 3 and every question over a pasted transcript were refused.
   The recording establishes the correlation and not the cause. It is the single
   biggest operational risk this file records: FIVE OF THIRTEEN TURNS WERE
   REFUSED BY THE VENDOR'S OWN SAFEGUARD, on prompts a wire's own preamble and
   respawn machinery will produce routinely.
